Some votes a national party just can't buy. The BJP is learning this the hard way in UP. Start with who the Kurmis are. - UP's second-largest OBC group after the Yadavs, about 7 to 10% of the state. - Packed tightly enough to decide 30 to 40 seats. - Backed the NDA for 10 years. - NDA's Kurmi vote has slid from 80% in 2019 to 66% in 2022 to 61% in 2024. You can see it in who got elected too. UP sent 11 Kurmi MPs to Parliament in 2024. Seven were from the Samajwadi Party. Only three were from the BJP. Here's the odd part. The BJP has an ally, Anupriya Patel's Apna Dal, whose whole job is to hold the Kurmi vote for it. The vote is leaving anyway. Why? Because the SP did something the BJP structurally couldn't. - SP let local Kurmi leaders build their own following. - It picked up district-level leaders from the BSP, gave them tickets, and ran them straight at the BJP. - In three seats it put up a Kurmi against a BJP Brahmin. It won all three. The BJP can't copy this easily. It's a national party with a fixed ideology. It won't bend to one caste, and it won't let a local leader grow into his own power centre. As one BJP leader put it – Kurmis follow their caste leaders, not a party. And the BJP makes it hard for such a leader to rise from inside. That's what the ally, Apna Dal, was for. But it only delivers around Mirzapur. Even there, Anupriya Patel's own win margin crashed from 2.3 lakh votes in 2019 to 38,000 in 2024. And now the ally is walking away from its own job. After some internal splits, Apna Dal has made a Dalit its state chief and told workers to stop being a Kurmi-only party. So the BJP did what national parties do. It fixed things from the top. In December it made a Kurmi MP, Pankaj Chaudhary, its state president. But his team looked handpicked by the central leadership, not by him, so the message fell flat. The lesson is bigger than one caste or one state. @nishthaanushree in @SwarajyaMag on why every fix the BJP has tried to fix the slide in Kurmi vote has failed, and what it means for 2027 — swarajyamag.com/uttar-prades…

نزدیک به پنج سال پس از بازگشت طالبان به قدرت در اسد ۱۴۰۰، ساختار اقتصادی افغانستان دستخوش تغییرات گسترده‌ای شده است. در میان نهادهایی که در این دوره جایگاه ویژه‌ای یافته‌اند، شرکت انکشاف ملی به‌عنوان بازوی اصلی اجرای پروژه‌های عمرانی حکومت، به یکی از مهم‌ترین بازیگران اقتصادی کشور تبدیل شده است. این شرکت که از ادغام چندین تصدی بزرگ دولتی شکل گرفته، امروز بخش قابل‌توجهی از فعالیت‌های ساختمانی، تولید مصالح و اجرای پروژه‌های زیربنایی را در اختیار دارد و عملا به یکی از بزرگ‌ترین مجموعه‌های اقتصادی وابسته به حکومت طالبان بدل شده است. بااین‌حال، روند گزارش‌دهی این شرکت در سال‌های اخیر با ابهام‌هایی همراه بوده است. شرکت انکشاف ملی در سال‌های نخست پس از تغییر نظام، اطلاعات مربوط به پروژه‌ها و وضعیت مالی خود را تا پایان سال ۲۰۲۳ در قالب گزارش‌های رسمی مکتوب منتشر می‌کرد، اما پس از آن، گزارش مالی جدید، ترازنامه یا جزئیات دقیقی درباره‌ی درآمدها، هزینه‌ها و عملکرد اقتصادی آن در دسترس عمومی قرار نگرفته است. این توقف در انتشار اطلاعات، پرسش‌هایی را درباره‌ی میزان شفافیت مالی، نحوه مدیریت منابع و سازوکارهای حساب‌دهی این نهاد بزرگ اقتصادی ایجاد کرده است. آخرین داده‌های مالی منتشرشده از سوی شرکت انکشاف ملی، مربوط به سال ۲۰۲۳، تصویری از ابعاد گسترده‌ی این مجموعه ارائه می‌کند. براساس اطلاعات رسمی منتشرشده در وب‌سایت این شرکت، ارزش دارایی‌های منقول و غیرمنقول آن بیش از ۵۴ میلیارد افغانی اعلام شده است. در کنار آن، ارزش مجموعی پروژه‌های تحت مدیریت شرکت به ۱۲۴ میلیارد افغانی می‌رسد؛ پروژه‌هایی که براساس همین گزارش‌ها، ۲۶.۸ میلیارد افغانی عواید ناخالص و ۱۱ میلیارد افغانی سود خالص ایجاد کرده‌اند. همچنین این شرکت حدود ۱۷.۵ میلیارد افغانی از وزارت‌خانه‌ها طلبکار اعلام شده است. ارزش پروژه‌های تحت مدیریت این شرکت، معادل نزدیک به یک‌چهارم بودجه‌ی عمومی سالانه‌ی افغانستان در سال‌های اخیر است. تنها دارایی‌های ثبت‌شده‌ی آن از بودجه‌ی انکشافی بسیاری از سال‌های حکومت پیشین نیز بیشتر است و سود خالص ۱۱ میلیارد افغانی آن با بودجه‌ی سالانه چندین وزارت‌خانه متوسط دولتی برابری می‌کند. این ارقام، که آخرین تصویر رسمی از وضعیت مالی شرکت پیش از توقف گزارش‌دهی عمومی به شمار می‌روند، ابعاد اقتصادی نهادی را نشان می‌دهند که در کم‌تر از چند سال به یکی از بزرگ‌ترین مراکز مدیریت دارایی و پروژه‌های حکومتی طالبان تبدیل شده است. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/257645

#ChinaSeen Nestled in the deserts of northwest China's Gansu Province, the #UNESCO World Heritage Mogao Caves are the world's largest and best-preserved Buddhist cave art site, with a collection of 735 caves spanning a cliff face 1,700 meters long. Among them are 492 caves housing paintings and sculptures dating back to the 4th century AD. Adorned with intricate murals, sculptures and architectural designs, they bear witness to the dynamic cultural exchanges along the Silk Road. The construction of the #MogaoCaves is generally believed to have begun sometime in the 4th century AD, when they served as places of Buddhist meditation for hermit monks. The caves continued to be expanded until the 14th century, eventually becoming places of worship and pilgrimage for the public. The Mogao Caves, an unparalleled treasure trove of ancient art, offer invaluable insight into the evolution of Chinese art, religious beliefs and daily life over the course of a millennium. Along with the Longmen Grottoes and the Yungang Grottoes, they are one of the three great ancient Buddhist sculptural sites in China. (Photos via VCG and IC) #ChinaTravel #CivilizationsShine

Ball (@deanwball) Some observations on Kimi: 1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run. 2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China. 3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "the art of not being governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex. 4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure." This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business. 5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this. 6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/deanwball/status/2078133895766114412#m

I'm a cardiologist. Everyone is sharing this study as a skin story. They're burying the part that matters. Scientists took the aorta of a 75-year-old donor, applied a single engineered enzyme, and stripped away more than 70% of the molecular damage — bringing it down to the levels you'd see in a 30-year-old artery. Published five days ago in Nature Communications. Revel Pharmaceuticals, with Calico and the University of Colorado. Here's what they erased. Sugar reacts with proteins in your body the same way heat browns bread — slowly, over a lifetime. It leaves behind a residue called CML, the most abundant advanced glycation end product in aging tissue. It welds itself onto collagen and elastin in your skin, your eye lens, and your arterial walls. Two things follow. Your arteries stiffen. And CML latches onto a receptor called RAGE, which drives chronic inflammation — the exact fire I've been writing about for months as the engine of heart disease. Since the 1980s this damage was considered permanent. Your body has no enzyme to remove it. Every existing approach only slows new damage from forming. Nothing touched what was already there. So they built an enzyme that doesn't exist in nature. They screened 45,000 protein structures, then ran five rounds of directed evolution across more than 500 million variants until they had CMLase — a molecular lawnmower that oxidizes the CML off the protein and restores the original, healthy lysine underneath. Not patched. Reversed. Over 70% cleared from elderly arterial tissue. Over 55% from elderly skin — below the levels found in 31-year-old skin. 45-78% in lens proteins. The CEO said they expected 20% and were floored. Arterial stiffness drives systolic hypertension, heart failure, and stroke, and I have no drug that reverses it. I can slow the process. I cannot undo it. This paper says undoing it may be possible. The caveats are real and I won't skip them. This was done on donated tissue in a dish, not in a living person. No functional data yet — we don't know if that artery got measurably more elastic. Delivering a large enzyme deep into human tissue is a hard, unsolved problem. Clinical trials are years away. But something considered permanent for forty years just came off human tissue. We spent a century learning to slow aging. Someone finally figured out how to erase it. Thank you @theallinpod @friedberg @chamath @pesottas The All-In Podcast (@theallinpod) Friedberg: New study shows enzyme reverses skin age from 70+ years to 31 Chamath: That’s a $2T market. Did Scientists Just Discover How to Reverse Skin Aging!? “CML is kind of the predominant molecule that gets formed in this extracellular matrix that's driving aging, and nothing breaks it down. So these scientists set out to try and create an enzyme, an enzyme is a protein that breaks something down, that can break down CML. And so these guys kind of went out and they took the target, which is CML, and tried to figure out, ‘Okay, how do we actually degrade CML, clear that extracellular matrix, and reverse aging?’ They started to test it on the proteins that we would find in our body, casein, collagen, retinal proteins, which are in your eye, hemoglobin, and they were able to get rid of 52 to 97% of the CML, just degrade it away. And then they found several sites where they were able to degrade over 90%. And then they took actual human skin from elderly patients that had donated their skin, and they put this enzyme onto that skin, and they were able to eliminate 55% of the CML on the skin, basically reverse the skin's age down to the age of a 31-year-old, this is from greater than 70-year-old patients, just by putting this enzyme on the skin. And so it's kind of a groundbreaking demonstration of combination of AlphaFold, what's called directed evolution, where you change the order of the DNA that changes the structure of the protein to test different proteins, do high throughput screening, and ultimately make a novel protein that doesn't exist in nature today that can do something pretty profound for human health.” Chamath: “It will be a trillion-dollar market. If you can create a cream…” Friedberg: “I mean, dude, if you could put this enzyme literally on your skin and have it absorb in…” Chamath: “Game over. That alone is $2 trillion.” Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/theallinpod/status/2078334237481046412#m

Trump Gives Green Light to Saudi Nuclear Program The Donald Trump administration has finalized the draft of a bilateral nuclear agreement that authorizes Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium on its own territory. Although the negotiating teams have completed the terms, the document still awaits Trump’s final signature and approval by the U.S. Congress. This framework breaks with the region’s long-standing non-proliferation rules. Unlike the deal with the United Arab Emirates, which permanently renounced uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing while accepting strict IAEA inspections, the agreement with the Saudis does not require Riyadh to adopt the Agency’s inspection regime. Oversight will be limited to a bilateral pact between the United States and Saudi Arabia. This reinforces what Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has already said openly: if Iran gets a nuclear weapon, Saudi Arabia will want one too. It sounds like a clear signal that Riyadh believes Tehran already has, or is very close to having, the bomb, which explains the intense pressure they are putting on Washington. The situation puts the U.S. in a complicated position. Saudi Arabia’s ballistic missile program is developed in partnership with China, complete with technology transfers. If the Americans don’t give in now, the Saudis have plenty of money to look for other partners. This is not just about civilian nuclear energy. For that, it would be enough to buy reactors and import ready-made fuel. What Riyadh really wants is to master the full nuclear fuel cycle, especially domestic uranium enrichment. With this infrastructure, Saudi Arabia is building a nuclear latency capability: it will control the core technology needed to develop a weapon in relatively short order if pushed by an existential threat. Weekend Ukraine map thread for Sunday 19th July 2026 Another focus on Crimea this weekend. Unmanned Systems have disabled much of the ferries operating across the strait, leaving two larger ferries being towed from Kavkaz to get supplies to the peninsula. Of course, a large amount of supply still arrives via the bridge disguised, but this is where we are with the heavy goods. Shipping in the Black Sea has been further disrupted with long range Firepoint strikes in the ringed area. The vessels have now dispersed from the anchorages, and are harder to strike but the damage has been done. Strikes here should settle down, similar to how the Sea of Azov strikes have settled due to a lack of targets. There are hundreds of new additions, we can only feature a few in the thread below. The full strikes can be seen on the map link in our bio. It is not just Crimea, there are strikes across the occupied territories from Mariupol to Luhansk. It is much more important than any political machinations going on right now. Elsewhere, there is not much to report that's actually changed land wise on the front. If you'd like us to give a focus on any specific area for you, please let us know. Russian strikes on Kyiv continue, and Russian strikes on Ukrainian shipping continue, so the Black Sea will likely not be useful for either side soon, a deal Ukraine is more than happy to make.

Islamabad: 14 July 2026. Ms. Michelle Bachelet, candidate for the position of the UN Secretary General, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House in Islamabad today. Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Sen. Muhammad Ishaq Dar and Foreign Secretary Amb. Amna Baloch were also present. While welcoming Ms. Bachelet to Pakistan, the Prime Minister reiterated Pakistan’s strong support for strengthening multilateralism as well as for ensuring the central role of the United Nations in addressing global challenges. The Prime Minister called for upholding the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations, faithful implementation of the UN resolutions and international treaties, as well as for achieving balanced progress across all three pillars of the United Nations - peace and security, development, and human rights. He also called for enhanced international cooperation and increased focus on accelerating the implementation of the global development agenda. Ms. Bachelet commended Pakistan's historic and invaluable contributions to the United Nations, and appreciated the country's ongoing contributions to regional and international peace and security. The fundamentals of the Iran War haven't changed since the first day of the war, and this is what makes continued escalation incredibly foolish for President Trump. Argue what you will about the ability for Iran to close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the irrefutable reality is that they can absolutely devastate Gulf energy and water infrastructure. One cannot reasonable assert otherwise. There is zero evidence whatsoever to support that the Iranian people are "so close" to rising up and toppling the regime. It failed miserably in January due to insufficient numbers, insufficient planning and coordination, and insufficient arming. Now, we've rallied Iran around the flag by bombing schoolchildren in Minab, threatening to wipe out their entire civilization, and a plethora of other missteps. No person without an insane degree of ideological extremism would say the Iranian regime has LESS support now than they did prior to the conflict. That is utterly absurd. The Iranian's have a FAR greater pain tolerance than the rest of the global economy does. This is an existential war for them, and an entirely optional war for the United States, and completely against the will of the rest of the world. We can not reopen the Strait of Hormuz through military power. We have tried this extensively through bombing campaigns and naval coordination via the Omani Route. We simply can not protect these vessels. These are the undeniable fundamentals of this conflict. They cannot rationally be argued against, nor are they remotely controversial. The FUNDAMENTALS show that continuing this escalation spiral is incredibly foolish for President Trump.

VIDEO | Delhi: Reacting to Rohit Sharma's 138-run knock at Lord's, his childhood coach Dinesh Lad says, "Two days ago, I spoke to him. I told him that I want to see him playing in the 2027 ODI World Cup, and I was confident that he would be there. Today, he showed everyone what he is capable of. There has been a lot of criticism that Rohit Sharma should retire-that he has done enough and that his time is over. I never agreed with that criticism. I always believed in his ability, and today he answered all his critics with his performance. The way he paced and constructed his innings today showed his experience, temperament and class. In my opinion, he has once again established himself as a strong contender to represent India in the 2027 ODI World Cup. Critics will always continue to criticise, but such things do not affect him. He remains focused on his cricket and on contributing to the team. He has already won the T20 World Cup and the Champions Trophy for India. One thing that has always stayed with him is the disappointment of missing out on the 2011 ODI World Cup squad and the heartbreak of India falling short in the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Ever since then, his biggest dream has been to win the 50-over World Cup for India. If India wants to lift the ODI World Cup next year, Rohit is a must-have in the team." America, from space. 🛰️ To celebrate America's 250th anniversary, the USGS has created a new portrait of the nation using imagery from Landsat 8 and Landsat 9. For more than 50 years, the @USGS and @NASA Landsat program has provided a continuous record of Earth's changing land surface. This new mosaic showcases the incredible diversity of the United States, from the rainforests of the Pacific Northwest to the Everglades of Florida, from the Rocky Mountains to the agricultural heartland of the Great Plains. It also continues a tradition that began in 1976, when Landsat imagery was used to create "Portrait U.S.A." for the nation's bicentennial. Pakistani media have reported that transit trade between Afghanistan and Pakistan fell to its lowest level in Pakistan's 2026 fiscal year, with its value dropping to just $367 million. According to the report, before 2021, transit trade between the two countries was worth around $5 billion, with approximately 89,000 containers transported annually. This year, however, the number of containers declined to about 11,600. The report noted that transit trade was at a strong level in 2023, when the number of containers exceeded 102,000 and the total trade value reached $6.7 billion. It said Afghanistan's shift toward Iran as an alternative transit route, along with the closure of crossings between Kabul and Islamabad, were among the main reasons for the sharp decline. The report further added that Afghanistan had already begun reducing its reliance on transit trade through Pakistan even before the crossings' closure, while seeking to expand trade and transit links with Iran and the Central Asian countries. #TOLOnews_English

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 received a call from the newly appointed Minister of Foreign Relations and Foreign Trade of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, H.E. Félix Plasencia. DPM/FM extended his warm congratulations to Minister Plasencia on his appointment. He conveyed Pakistan’s heartfelt condolences over the devastating earthquakes that recently struck Venezuela. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with the Government and the people of Venezuela during this difficult time and expressed confidence in their resilience and recovery. Minister Plasencia thanked DPM/FM for Pakistan’s message of sympathy and solidarity. He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support and humanitarian solidarity with the victims of the natural disasters, underscoring the importance of mutual support in times of need. He further acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the regional situation involving the United States and Iran and commended its commitment to peace and diplomacy. The two Ministers exchanged views on the longstanding friendly relations between Pakistan and Venezuela and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties. They discussed opportunities to expand cooperation across a broad range of sectors, including trade, investment, business, agriculture, IT, and other areas of mutual interest. Both sides underscored the considerable potential for enhancing economic collaboration and fostering stronger people-to-people contacts for the mutual benefit of the two countries. DPM/FM emphasized the importance of sustained high-level engagement to reinvigorate bilateral relations and further deepen cooperation. Both sides appreciated the continued close coordination between Pakistan and Venezuela at multilateral forums on issues of common interest. They agreed to remain in close contact and to meet at the earliest appropriate opportunity. @Cancilleria_ve

Mufti Taqi Usmani has declared purchasing goods with cryptocurrency “impermissible”, citing research conducted by experts so far which found that cryptocurrency does not qualify as “wealth”. The fatwa was originally issued by Darul Ifta, Jamia Darul Uloom, Karachi, and dated 24 Zilhaj 1447 AH (June 10, 2026). I don’t know which experts but I am not aware of any individuals in Pakistan, who are known as experts on cryptocurrencies, which is a fast evolving financial product. Leaving aside this issue of competence, I believe some important questions need to be asked about Mufti Taqi Usmani's public role and legacy. Mufti Taqi Usmani's judicial career began during General Zia-ul-Haq's military dictatorship. In 1982, he was appointed by Zia to the Federal Shariat Court, at a time when Pakistan was under martial law and democratic institutions had been weakened. To understand the significance of that appointment, one must understand the politics of the Zia era. Islamization was not merely a programme of legal reform; it became a central source of legitimacy for a military government that had seized power through a coup and removed an elected prime minister through what has now been established as judicial murder. Religious laws, institutions, and symbolism became closely intertwined with the state's political project. This process fundamentally reshaped Pakistan's legal and social landscape, and its consequences remain the subject of intense debate. The Federal Shariat Court was established within this broader context as a key institution for reviewing laws against Islamic injunctions. Appointments to the court were therefore not simply routine judicial appointments; they were part of a wider transformation of Pakistan's legal order. Mufti Taqi Usmani's role in that transformation deserves examination not because he was a religious scholar, but because he occupied a position of significant judicial authority at a historically consequential moment. Some of his judgments also had major economic and social implications. A prominent example is the Qazalbash Waqf case, decided by the Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court in 1989, in which Mufti Taqi Usmani authored the majority opinion. The judgment held that key aspects of Pakistan's land reform framework, particularly restrictions on land ownership, were inconsistent with Islamic principles. The significance of this judgment was highlighted by senior lawyer Abid Hasan Minto, former President of the Supreme Court Bar Association, who argued that the issue was not merely about property rights but about the structure of economic and political power in Pakistan. He placed the decision in the context of Pakistan's long-standing agrarian inequality and the continued influence of large landholders, arguing that weakening land reform efforts had consequences far beyond a legal dispute. For critics, therefore, the Qazalbash Waqf judgment was not simply a matter of interpreting religious principles; it was a decision with profound implications for Pakistan's social structure, rural inequality, and the concentration of political power among large landholding elites. Supporters viewed the decision as a defence of private property rights. Critics argued that it weakened attempts to address Pakistan's highly unequal agrarian structure and protected the interests of large landholders. This remains an important debate because land ownership has shaped Pakistan's economic inequality and political power for generations. The second issue is Islamic banking. Mufti Taqi Usmani has been one of the most influential figures in the development and certification of modern Islamic finance. Through his association with institutions including Meezan Bank and other Islamic financial entities, he has played a major role in shaping an industry that has become a significant part of Pakistan's banking sector. However, Islamic banking itself deserves serious scrutiny and debate. This criticism is not limited to religious critics. Former finance minister Dr Miftah Ismail recently argued that much of modern Islamic banking has become "more in nomenclature and less in substance." He questioned whether many products genuinely reflect the principles of risk-sharing and partnership that Islamic finance originally promised, or whether they often replicate conventional banking outcomes through different contractual structures. This debate is not about faith. It is about whether practical outcomes match stated principles. When religious scholars play central roles in approving financial products and providing Shariah certification to commercial institutions, questions about governance and transparency are entirely legitimate. What advisory roles exist? What compensation arrangements are in place? What disclosure standards apply? How are potential conflicts of interest managed? How independent can oversight be when the institutions being overseen provide compensation for that oversight? These are not accusations. They are normal questions of corporate governance, particularly where publicly listed institutions are involved. Indeed, if Islamic finance claims to represent a higher ethical standard than conventional finance, then transparency and accountability should be its defining characteristics. My concern is not with religious belief. It is with power without accountability. No one — whether a politician, general, judge, banker, academic, or religious scholar — should be beyond scrutiny. Respect for scholarship does not require intellectual submission. Religious credentials do not create immunity from questions. Public influence brings public responsibility. And the uncomfortable questions are often the ones that matter most.

EL MUNDIAL DE LAS APUESTAS: DURANTE EL TORNEO, LOS “MERCADOS DE PREDICCIÓN” MOVILIZARON MÁS DE USD 50 MIL MILLONES Kalshi, Polymarket y Rothera concentraron enormes sumas en operaciones ligadas al torneo, disputando terreno a las casas de juego tradicionales, que también reportaron cifras récord El Mundial 2026 dejó una marca que va más allá del resultado deportivo. De acuerdo con un relevamiento publicado por CoinDesk, las plataformas de mercados de predicción se convirtieron en uno de los protagonistas económicos del torneo, con volúmenes de negociación que rivalizaron e incluso superaron a los de las casas de apuestas deportivas tradicionales en Estados Unidos. Kalshi, una de las plataformas más activas del sector, alcanzó en junio un volumen nominal total de 31.000 millones de dólares, un salto de más del 70% respecto de mayo. Según datos de la firma de análisis Dune citados por el medio, los contratos vinculados al deporte representaron cerca del 85% de esa negociación. La empresa precisó además que el volumen específico asociado al Mundial en su plataforma llegó a 22.420 millones de dólares. El resto del sector también mostró cifras elevadas. Polymarket, el exchange internacional de mercados de predicción, marcó un récord mensual con 10.800 millones de dólares negociados, mientras que su versión regulada para el mercado estadounidense sumó otros 3.500 millones, casi el doble de lo registrado en mayo. A ese panorama se sumó Rothera, la plataforma lanzada en junio por Robinhood y Susquehanna International Group, que en su primer mes de operación procesó 2.000 millones de dólares y ya concentra el 7% del mercado de predicciones en Estados Unidos, según estimaciones de Bank of America difundidas por CoinDesk. 🔗infob.ae/4fc1STk

Competition between US and Chinese AI models is heating up: The proportion of tokens used by US firms that run through Chinese AI models on OpenRouter is up to a record ~58%. OpenRouter is a platform that allows developers and companies to access and compare AI models from multiple providers, making it a useful gauge of real-world AI model adoption. This percentage has TRIPLED since mid-January, overtaking American peers on the platform for the first time in March. The token share of Chinese models briefly rose as high as 63% in the first week of July. By comparison, Chinese models accounted for less than 10% of usage at the start of 2025, while US models accounted for ~80%. DeepSeek has emerged as the most popular choice among American firms in recent months. Chinese AI models are rapidly gaining market share.

“Hermanos para siempre” 🥹 Antonio Banderas (@antoniobanderas) Hola amigos. Hoy es la final del Campeonato del Mundo de Fútbol. Naturalmente quiero que gane España, pero también el fútbol y todo aquello que une a nuestros dos países. Durante un rato España y Argentina serán rivales. Después volverán a ser lo que siempre han sido para mí: dos pueblos hermanos. Quizá suene tonto decir esto, pero siento la necesidad de expresar que, pase lo que pase, yo seguiré admirando a los inmensos artistas argentinos con los que he tenido el privilegio de trabajar, seguiré admirando a sus jugadores de fútbol y, por supuesto, seguiré queriendo a mis muchos amigos de Argentina y a todo un país al que me siento profundamente unido. El deporte tiene esa maravillosa capacidad de enfrentarnos sin dividirnos, de competir sin dejar de respetarnos y de recordarnos que la verdadera victoria nunca debería pertenecer al odio, sino a la admiración. Que gane quien mejor juegue. Y que, cuando el árbitro señale el final, celebremos todos algo mucho más importante que un resultado: la amistad entre dos países que hablan el mismo idioma, y la oportunidad que nos da la vida para con el buen comportamiento de jugadores e hinchas, de dar ejemplo, de enorgullecer y hacer brillar a las comunidades hispanas de todo el mundo. श्री विवेक अग्रवाल, सचिव, संस्कृति मंत्रालय ने आज राष्ट्रीय पुस्तकालय, बेलवेडियर में भारत के प्रथम ‘शब्द संग्रहालय’ के लोकार्पण समारोह में स्वागत संबोधन के दौरान कहा कि यह संग्रहालय माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi के विजन के अनुरूप स्थापित किया गया है। संग्रहालय में ध्वनि से शब्द, शब्द से भाषा और भाषा से लिपि के विकास की यात्रा तथा ब्राह्मी और खरोष्ठी जैसी प्राचीन लिपियों के वैश्विक प्रभाव को प्रदर्शित किया गया है। साथ ही, इस दौरान श्री अग्रवाल ने यह भी जानकारी साझा की कि संस्कृति मंत्रालय द्वारा ‘ज्ञान भारतम मिशन’ के अंतर्गत अब तक 1 करोड़ 18 लाख से अधिक पांडुलिपियों की पहचान की जा चुकी है और उनके डिजिटलीकरण का कार्य जारी है। संस्कृति सचिव ज्ञान भारतम के महत्त्व को रेखांकित करते हुए कहते हैं कि ‘ज्ञान भारतम’ इस संग्रहालय की वास्तविक आत्मा और मूल भावना है। उन्होंने विश्वास व्यक्त किया कि ‘शब्द संग्रहालय’ के प्रथम चरण की यह शुरुआत ‘ज्ञान भारतम’ के माध्यम से भारत की ज्ञान परंपरा को और अधिक प्रभावी ढंग से आगे बढ़ाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाएगी। #MuseumOfWord #CultureUnitesAll Video

Dr. Joram Aniya, Member, NITI Aayog, called on Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, during her visit to the State to discuss key priorities for sustainable development, and long-term growth. The discussions focused on enhancing disaster preparedness and resilient infrastructure while exploring collaboration in school education, tourism, culture, youth affairs, and sports. Emphasis was laid on integrating disaster risk reduction into development planning and addressing the unique geographical and climatic challenges of the North Eastern States. Dr. Joram Aniya also proposed organising a National Workshop on Sustainable Tourism in Arunachal Pradesh in November 2026 to promote community-based tourism, showcase the State’s rich cultural and natural heritage, and unlock new avenues for sustainable economic growth. स्टार्टअप इंडिया मिशन: सपनों से सफलता तक, भारत की नई उड़ान...🚀🇮🇳 एक समय था जब साल 2014 से पहले देश का युवा सिर्फ नौकरी पाने का सपना देखता था। प्रतिभा थी, विचार थे, लेकिन उन्हें आगे बढ़ाने के लिए न पूंजी थी, न अनुकूल नीतियां और न ही ऐसा माहौल जो उद्यमिता को प्रोत्साहित कर सके। लेकिन साल 2014 में श्री @narendramodi के प्रधानमंत्री बनने के बाद भारत ने एक नई सोच अपनाई— "अब युवा केवल Job Seekers नहीं, बल्कि Job Creators भी बनेंगे।" इसी सोच को साकार करने के लिए 16 जनवरी 2016 को शुरू हुआ स्टार्टअप इंडिया मिशन, जिसने भारत में उद्यमिता की तस्वीर बदल दी। आज की ये उपलब्धियां बताती हैं कि यह बदलाव कितना बड़ा है- ✅ 2.23 लाख+ DPIIT मान्यता प्राप्त स्टार्टअप्स ✅ 23.36 लाख+ प्रत्यक्ष रोजगार का सृजन ✅ 10,000 करोड़ रुपये का Fund of Funds Framework ✅ मजबूत Seed Funding Ecosystem ✅ 1.07 लाख+ स्टार्टअप्स में कम से कम एक महिला निदेशक/साझेदार ✅ Digital India और UPI के माध्यम से मजबूत डिजिटल आधार ✅ भारत दुनिया का तीसरा सबसे बड़ा स्टार्टअप इकोसिस्टम बनने की दिशा में अग्रसर वर्ष 2025-26 भी इस यात्रा का एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव रहा। केवल एक वित्तीय वर्ष में 55,200+ नए स्टार्टअप्स को मान्यता मिली, स्टार्टअप रिकॉग्निशन में 51.6% और प्रत्यक्ष रोजगार में 36.1% की वृद्धि दर्ज की गई। यह केवल आंकड़ों की कहानी नहीं, बल्कि उन लाखों युवाओं की सफलता की कहानी है, जिन्होंने अपने विचारों को उद्यम में बदला, रोजगार के नए अवसर बनाए और भारत को वैश्विक नवाचार के मानचित्र पर नई पहचान दिलाई। आज भारत में स्टार्टअप केवल एक व्यवसाय नहीं, बल्कि आत्मनिर्भर भारत, नवाचार और रोजगार सृजन की मजबूत नींव बन चुके हैं। Video

WSJ: THE SAVE AMERICA ACT BACKFIRE In a floor speech Thursday, North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis argued that even if Congress whooped through the bill, there isn’t time to implement it before November. By his reckoning, the U.S. has about 10,000 county clerks or municipal entities that carry out America’s decentralized elections. The midterms are barely 100 days away, early voting sooner. “The math doesn’t work,” he said. “It can’t be done.” Mr. Tillis isn’t against ID rules, and he helped pass North Carolina’s. “We should figure out a way to get every state to get to voter ID,” he said. Yet he was unsparing toward Congress’s proponents of the SAVE America Act. “Mr. President, these people are misleading you if they’re telling you that this can be implemented by November,” he said. “This seems like a legit proposal, but it isn’t.” Unfortunately, the message from Mr. Trump and others has been that America’s elections can’t be trusted, and the only hope is the SAVE America Act. Aside from being untrue, this is a political backfire for the GOP. If Republican voters believe it, and the bill falls short, then why waste time going to the polls in November? Sandra Joyce, VP Google Threat Intelligence, spent the past year arguing that disrupting adversary infrastructure has to become normal practice. She’s right. January 2026: Google's threat intel team and partners dismantled IPIDEA, the world's largest residential proxy network. Google counted 550+ distinct threat groups using it, including state actors from China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran. Court orders killed the storefronts and 7,400+ C2 servers went dark. Monday July 13, 2026: The EU and UK rolled out their first-ever joint cyber sanctions package against Russia. Scott Jasper’s study of Russian cyber operations says it bluntly: sanctions and indictments have “done little to alter Moscow’s behavior.” You can't freeze assets that were never here. You can't arrest a GRU officer who never leaves Moscow. Sanctioning at that scale is record-keeping, not deterrence. What will actually degrade an adversary? Joyce's point is that the private sector IS the infrastructure adversaries abuse. Private tech companies own the infrastructure, the platforms, apps, and networks, that these attacks run on, and they can shut an operation down directly and immediately. The most useful thing government can do is to build the legal scaffolding that lets the private sector run these operations at scale. My own proposal is more controversial: a licensed cyber letter of marque system (think bounty hunters for cybercrime) requiring congressional authorization, for limited private-sector offensive operations under strict oversight. If you don’t run a hyperscaler, none of this sounds like yours to act on. It is. For defenders who aren't Google: robtlee73.substack.com/p/san… Tell me where you land on this. And would the letter of marque idea go too far for you? I want the argument.

Developed by the Ministry of Culture and situated at the historic Belvedere House within the National Library campus, it is India's first immersive language museum and explores the country's rich linguistic & storytelling traditions. The museum features nine interactive galleries equipped with advanced technologies such as hand-gesture sensors, acoustic hallways, and radio frequency identification (RFID) devices. The Minister also extended his best wishes to the Ambassador for her happiness, success, and prosperity in her future endeavours.

U.S. Embassy Amman (@USEmbassyJordan) Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Amman - July 19. 2026 Due to a specific and credible threat, Jordanian authorities evacuated the international airport and seaport in Aqaba. We strongly advise all Americans to refrain traveling to either the airport or seaport. Continue to follow all Jordanian authorities’ security directives. U.S. Embassy Amman continues to advise all Americans to avoid travel to military bases in Jordan. On March 2, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members to leave Jordan due to safety risks. Actions to Take: Please visit Jordan’s National Center for Security and Crisis Management website for public safety guidelines, including explanations of emergency sirens in Jordan. Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings. Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence. Monitor local media. Follow the instructions of local authorities. Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected. Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States. Keep a low profile. Enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment connects you to the U.S. embassy or consulate so you get the latest security updates. It also makes it easier for the U.S. Embassy or consulate to contact you in an emergency. When it comes to protecting the lives and livelihoods of our people, there is no Government or Opposition only Sri Lanka. Today, at the National Council for Disaster Management chaired by H.E the President, I shared a strategic science-backed proposal to help Sri Lanka prepare for the anticipated climate risks of 2026–27. My message was simple; we cannot afford to wait for disaster to strike we must act. By strengthening early warning systems, safeguarding our food and water security, and planning together as a nation, we can create greater resilience against climate change. NewsWire 🇱🇰 (@NewsWireLK) Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed a series of measures to strengthen Sri Lanka’s climate resilience and disaster preparedness, warning that the country should act now to prepare for the anticipated impacts of the 2026-2027 El Niño cycle. Speaking at the National Council for Disaster Management, chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Premadasa said climate security has become a national priority that requires a united, science-based response beyond political differences. Citing global scientific assessments, Premadasa warned that the developing El Niño could be among the strongest in recent decades, bringing prolonged droughts followed by severe flooding. He said Sri Lanka should move away from responding to disasters after they occur and instead adopt an anticipatory governance model based on scientific forecasting, risk assessments and early preparedness. Among his key proposals was making climate resilience a whole-of-government responsibility involving institutions responsible for agriculture, water resources, energy, health, finance, defence, provincial administration and local government. Premadasa also called for integrated reservoir management to improve water security, expansion of climate-smart agriculture to strengthen food security, and the modernisation of early warning systems through impact-based forecasting that provides communities with more actionable information before disasters strike. He further proposed strengthening disaster risk financing, improving preparedness for heatwaves and public health emergencies, enhancing the resilience of critical infrastructure, and establishing a National Climate Risk and Disaster Intelligence Centre to support evidence-based decision-making across Government. Premadasa said Sri Lanka should also draw lessons from countries such as India and Australia, which have strengthened climate forecasting, agricultural contingency planning and broader resilience initiatives in response to growing climate risks. Looking beyond the immediate El Niño threat, he proposed the preparation of a Presidential White Paper on National Climate Resilience and Disaster Preparedness to establish a long-term policy framework that would guide future governments. He stressed that climate resilience cannot be achieved by the Government alone and requires the participation of Parliament, provincial and local authorities, the scientific community, universities, the private sector, civil society, international development partners and local communities. Premadasa added that protecting the lives and livelihoods of Sri Lankans must remain a shared national responsibility. رسانه‌های پاکستانی گزارش داده‌اند که تجارت ترانزیت افغانستان و پاکستان در سال مالی ۲۰۲۶ پاکستان، به پایین‌ترین سطح خود رسیده و ارزش آن تنها ۳۶۷میلیون دالر بوده است. بر بنیاد این گزارش، ارزش تجارت ترانزیت میان دو کشور پیش از سال ۲۰۲۱ به حدود پنج میلیارد دالر می‌رسید و سالانه نزدیک به ۸۹هزار کانتینر میان دو کشور جابه‌جا می‌شد؛ اما این رقم در سال جاری به حدود ۱۱ هزار و ۶۰۰ کانتینر کاهش یافته است. بر پایه گزارش، تجارت ترانزیت میان افغانستان و پاکستان در سال ۲۰۲۳ از وضعیت مطلوبی برخوردار بود؛ به‌گونه‌ای که شمار کانتینرها از ۱۰۲ هزار فراتر رفت و ارزش آن ۶.۷ میلیارد دالر گزارش شد. در این گزارش آمده است که روی‌آوردن افغانستان به ایران به‌عنوان مسیر بدیل و نیز مسدود ماندن گذرگاه‌ها میان کابل و اسلام‌آباد، از عوامل اصلی این کاهش به شمار می‌روند. این گزارش همچنین می‌افزاید که افغانستان حتی پیش از بسته‌شدن گذرگاه‌ها نیز تجارت ترانزیت خود با پاکستان را کاهش داده و در پی گسترش همکاری‌های ترانزیتی و تجاری با ایران و کشورهای آسیای مرکزی بوده است. #طلوع‌نیوز

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 received a call from the newly appointed Minister of Foreign Relations and Foreign Trade of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, H.E. Félix Plasencia. DPM/FM extended his warm congratulations to Minister Plasencia on his appointment. He conveyed Pakistan’s heartfelt condolences over the devastating earthquakes that recently struck Venezuela. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with the Government and the people of Venezuela during this difficult time and expressed confidence in their resilience and recovery. Minister Plasencia thanked DPM/FM for Pakistan’s message of sympathy and solidarity. He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support and humanitarian solidarity with the victims of the natural disasters, underscoring the importance of mutual support in times of need. He further acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the regional situation involving the United States and Iran and commended its commitment to peace and diplomacy. The two Ministers exchanged views on the longstanding friendly relations between Pakistan and Venezuela and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties. They discussed opportunities to expand cooperation across a broad range of sectors, including trade, investment, business, agriculture, IT, and other areas of mutual interest. Both sides underscored the considerable potential for enhancing economic collaboration and fostering stronger people-to-people contacts for the mutual benefit of the two countries. DPM/FM emphasized the importance of sustained high-level engagement to reinvigorate bilateral relations and further deepen cooperation. Both sides appreciated the continued close coordination between Pakistan and Venezuela at multilateral forums on issues of common interest. They agreed to remain in close contact and to meet at the earliest appropriate opportunity. @Cancilleria_ve

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 received a telephone call today from the Foreign Minister of the State of Kuwait, H.E. Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah. The two Foreign Ministers discussed the latest developments in the region. Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah shared Kuwait’s serious concerns regarding the continued attacks on its territory and expressed hope that restraint would be exercised by all sides and that the Islamabad MoU would be fully implemented. Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah also appreciated Pakistan’s constructive and mediatory role in promoting dialogue and regional stability. The Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister underscored the urgent need for de-escalation, stressed the importance of respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states, and emphasized that maintaining regional peace and security must remain the foremost priority. He also underlined the importance of upholding ceasefire commitments under the Islamabad MoU and avoiding any actions that could further escalate tensions. The two leaders agreed to remain in close contact on matters of mutual interest. @MOFAKuwait

𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐆𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐒' 𝟏𝟗𝟔𝟗 𝐁𝐀𝐍𝐊 𝐍𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐀𝐋𝐈𝐒𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍: 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐑𝐎𝐎𝐓 𝐎𝐅 𝐈𝐍𝐃𝐈𝐀'𝐒 𝐍𝐏𝐀 𝐂𝐑𝐈𝐒𝐈𝐒 On this day in 1969, the Congress government led by Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 major commercial banks through the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance. Presented as a step toward socialism and financial inclusion, the decision fundamentally altered India's banking system. With nearly 85% of the country's banking deposits brought under government control, lending increasingly became vulnerable to political influence. Commercial banking gradually gave way to politically directed credit, where loans were often sanctioned to fulfil populist objectives rather than sound financial assessment. This marked the beginning of the "loan mela" culture, weakening credit discipline and institutional autonomy. Over the following decades, politically motivated lending, inadequate risk evaluation, and poor recovery mechanisms contributed to the build-up of massive Non-Performing Assets (NPAs), burdening public sector banks and ultimately costing taxpayers dearly. I can confirm that throughout 2023–2024 we suffered enormous losses because of repeated counterattacks to retake tree lines and ruins, and it all followed the same pattern. Our troops occupied advantageous positions and destroyed the enemy as if at a shooting range. Enemy losses were 17–25 times greater than ours. But then "someone" decided the line on the map wasn't neat enough, and the endless orders began: "straighten the line," "retake the previously lost positions." The result was losses that were impossible to justify, with two consequences. First, the casualty ratio dropped to only three to one. Second, our infantry was often too small in number and disoriented, allowing the enemy to break through not only the "retaken positions" but also the previously stable defensive line where they had earlier failed again and again despite enormous losses. This is how we lost an enormous number of people—so many that, had they been preserved, there would have been far less need for new mobilization. The second recurring pattern was the rotations in 2023–2024. During these rotations, the enemy struck newly arrived units and broke through. These constant rotations to patch holes elsewhere, with breakthroughs as the inevitable consequence, were also characteristic of Syrskyi's style. Any other army in the same situation would have assigned sectors of responsibility to large formations—divisions, corps, armies—and reinforced them with fresh battalions. Instead, we saw the constant creation of new units and endless crisis micromanagement instead of an overall strategy. By 2025–2026, this entire Syrskyi-style way of fighting had become impossible because of drones. Yet attempts to continue fighting this way have not stopped. Fighting through unjustified losses and constant micromanagement without sustained support has simply become a habit. If earlier this approach cost us Ocheretyne, now it is Siversk. The strategy remains the same: weaken our own forces and allow the enemy to gain the advantage. Anyone would have replaced General Syrskyi long ago with someone more capable. Anyone would also have sought the advice of a trusted military adviser instead of reacting emotionally and trying to command military professionals directly. At the end of 1942, Stalin recognized the brilliance of General Antonov, whose phenomenal memory impressed him, and made him his principal adviser. It was precisely because Stalin listened to Antonov that the victories which followed became possible. Antonov also had the courage to tell Stalin the truth in private, although after the war Stalin's pride resurfaced, and he sent Antonov away to the provinces in 1948. Churchill and Roosevelt tested generals and replaced them until they found commanders who did not merely fight, but who won. Once they found winners, they tolerated them despite all their eccentricities. Today, in the era of drone warfare, we objectively need a different kind of war than the one fought under Syrskyi and Zelenskyy in previous years. We need a different team of generals capable of winning the war that is being fought today, because Syrskyi's methods lead toward defeat once the enemy completes its mobilization. And we must have the patience to trust new generals instead of interfering with their command. Biden Appointee’s Impressive En Banc Ruling on Second Amendment and ‘Assault Firearms’ Yesterday the en banc Third Circuit ruled (in Association of New Jersey Rifle and Pistol Clubs v. Attorney General) that New Jersey’s ban on so-called “assault firearms” and its restrictions on possession of “large capacity ammunition magazines” (LCMs) violate the Second Amendment. Judge Arianna J. Freeman, appointed by Joe Biden in 2022, wrote the impressive majority opinion for eight judges. (Or perhaps I should say for ten judges, since a ninth states that she “fully support[s] the majority opinion” and a tenth that he joins the majority opinion “in nearly every respect.”) Five judges dissented. I am not going to summarize the 192 pages of opinions here. I’ll make just a few observations: 1. In addition to composing a powerful 60-page opinion, Judge Freeman demonstrated real courage in departing from the Left’s tenaciously held party line against Second Amendment rights. She could easily have voted to defer ruling on the matter on the ground that the issue will be decided by the Supreme Court next term (in the consolidated cases of Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins). But she refused to take that path. Freeman also might have gone no further than to affirm the district court’s ruling that New Jersey’s ban on Colt AR-45s violates the Second Amendment. But she instead determined that “the record supports the same result for all semi-automatic rifles,” so she broadened the district court’s order to cover all semi-automatic rifles covered by the New Jersey ban. In concluding that the LCM restrictions violate the Second Amendment, she also rejected the district court’s conclusion. As a young (47 or 48 years old) African American appellate judge with a Yale law school pedigree, Freeman has been touted as a strong candidate for a Supreme Court nomination by the next Democrat president. As Freeman surely knew, her ruling has destroyed her chances of ever being nominated to the Court. The Left is livid over the ruling, and its anger is intensified by Freeman’s lead role in it. According to New Jersey attorney general Jennifer Davenport, who called the ruling “as unfortunate as it is legally incorrect,” “every other federal circuit court to consider the issue has come out the other way.” Any effort to depict the Second Amendment argument against bans on “assault firearms” as extreme is severely undercut not just by Freeman’s opinion but by who she is. High blood pressure - or #hypertension - often shows no warning signs, yet it increases the risk for heart disease, stroke, blindness, dementia, and other complications. A simple blood pressure check can be life-saving. Getting your blood pressure measured the right way helps ensure accurate results. Incorrect positions can lead to incorrect readings. ✔ Sit with your back supported ✔ Legs uncrossed and feet flat on the floor ✔ Arm supported with the cuff at heart level ✔ Use correct cuff size ✔ Rest for at least 5 minutes before the reading ✔ Do not talk during or between measurements ✔ Avoid exercise, tea/coffee, and smoking for at least 30 minutes before reading Small steps can make a big difference in protecting your health.

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif’s Message on the Occasion of Youm-e-Ilhaq-e-Pakistan (Kashmir’s Accession to Pakistan Day) 19 July 2026. Youm-e-Ilhaq-e-Pakistan (Kashmir’s Accession to Pakistan Day) is observed annually to commemorate the historic resolution adopted by the All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference at its Srinagar session on 19 July 1947. The unanimous resolution reflected the collective political aspirations of the Muslims of Jammu and Kashmir at a defining moment in the history of the subcontinent. It expressed their desire for the State’s accession to Pakistan and called upon the Dogra rulers to respect the will of the people. The resolution remains an important historical milestone in the political struggle of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. This occasion also serves as a reminder of the enduring bonds that unite the peoples of Pakistan and Jammu and Kashmir, founded on shared history, faith, culture, geography and longstanding ties. Above all, it underscores the central importance of respecting the freely expressed will of the Kashmiri people. Pakistan remains steadfast in its principled support for the inalienable right to self-determination of the people of Jammu and Kashmir, as enshrined in the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. The unresolved Jammu and Kashmir dispute continues to have profound implications for regional peace and security. Lasting peace in South Asia requires its peaceful resolution in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. The Government and people of Pakistan salute the courage, resilience and steadfastness of the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) in their just struggle for the realization of their fundamental rights. Pakistan will continue to extend its unwavering diplomatic, political and moral support until the people of Jammu and Kashmir are able to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination.

Luton, UK: Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri Delivers Keynote Address at "Shan-e-Ahl-e-Bait-e-Nabvi ﷺ Conference" His Eminence Shaykh-ul-Islam Dr Muhammad Tahir-ul-Qadri, founding leader of Minhaj-ul-Quran International, delivered the keynote address at the "Shan-e-Ahl-e-Bait-e-Nabviﷺ Conference", organised on the occasion of the "Ta'ziyati Reference of Pir Syed Abdul Qadir Shah Jillani (R.A)" under the auspices of Markazi Jama'at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas) at Jamia Islamia Ghousia Trust, Luton. Addressing a large gathering of scholars, community leaders and students of knowledge, Shaykh-ul-Islam delivered a profound Qur’anic exposition of Ayat al-Tatheer (The Verse of Purification) from Surah al-Ahzab (33:33): اِنَّمَا یُرِیْدُ اللهُ لِیُذْهِبَ عَنْکُمُ الرِّجْسَ اَهْلَ الْبَیْتِ وَیُطَہِّرَکُمْ تَطْہِیْرًا “Stay in your homes and do not display your charm, like the displaying of the former (days of) ignorance. Establish the prayer, pay the alms due and keep obeying Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). Indeed, Allah only desires to keep all (forms and causes of) impurity away from you, O Members of the (Prophet’s) Family, and purify you with a thorough purifying.” Shaykh-ul-Islam explained that this blessed verse is a clear and unequivocal declaration of the unique rank, spiritual excellence and divinely bestowed purity of the blessed Ahl al-Bayt (ʿalayhim al-salām). He stated that Almighty Allah Himself has declared His exclusive will to remove every form of rijs—including every impurity, spiritual defect, doubt, moral corruption and anything contrary to goodness—and to grant them complete and perfect taṭhīr. Explaining the Qur’anic language, Shaykh-ul-Islam emphasised that the verse is not merely a command for the Ahl al-Bayt to attain purity through their own efforts. Rather, it is a decisive declaration that Allah ﷻ Himself undertook their complete purification. This divine act establishes their honour, purity and spiritual rank through the Qur’an itself. He further explained that the emphatic expression “وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا” signifies not an ordinary form of purification but a complete, perfect and divinely bestowed purification encompassing every aspect of their belief, intentions, character, conduct, sacrifice and spiritual excellence. He stressed that the sacrifices of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the events of Karbala, must be understood through this Qur’anic declaration rather than through political or worldly interpretations. Elaborating on the unparalleled virtues and elevated status of the Ahl al-Bayt in the light of the Holy Qur’an and authentic Prophetic traditions, Shaykh-ul-Islam affirmed that love, reverence and loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt are fundamental to the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah. He urged believers to return to the Qur’an and Sunnah when understanding their status and warned against allowing polemics or distorted historical narratives to shape their perception. He described the blessed Household of the Holy Prophet ﷺ as the purest embodiment of his guidance, character and spiritual legacy, whose lives continue to illuminate the path of faith, knowledge, piety and moral excellence. The conference was attended by Pir Syed Mazhar Hussain Gillani, President of Markazi Jama’at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas); Pir Syed Munawar Hussain Shah Jamati; Syed Ali Abbas Bukhari, President of Minhaj-ul-Quran International UK; Allama Qazi Abdul Aziz Chishti MBE, Secretary General of Markazi Jama’at-e-Ahle Sunnat (UK & Overseas); alongside distinguished scholars, community leaders and members of the Muslim community from across the United Kingdom. The gathering concluded with collective prayers for the unity of the Muslim Ummah and for peace, stability and prosperity throughout the world. #AhlulBayt #ProphetMuhammad #ShaykhUlIslam #DrTahirulQadri #Luton #IslamicEvent #UKMuslims #MarkaziJamaatEAhleSunnat #LoveForAhlulBayt #MQIUK

I'm genuinely confused by the argument here. It seems to be: open-weight AI models reduce the profits of American VC-backed companies; many leading open models currently come from China; therefore open AI is somehow "communist." We've never applied that logic to any other technology. Linux, Apache, PostgreSQL, and countless other open-source projects destroyed proprietary software margins and dramatically reduced returns for some investors. We called that competition and innovation—not communism. If the concern is reliance on Chinese AI, make that argument. If the concern is national security, make that argument. But "this technology makes it harder for incumbents to earn monopoly-like returns" has never been a definition of communism. It's often just what technological progress and real free markets look like. Dean W. Ball (@deanwball) Some observations on Kimi: 1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run. 2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China. 3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "the art of not being governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex. 4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure." This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business. 5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this. 6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/deanwball/status/2078133895766114412#m

आज पश्चिम बंगाल के सिलीगुड़ी में भारत-बांग्लादेश सीमा से जुड़े सुरक्षा मुद्दों पर बैठक की। मोदी सरकार सीमावर्ती क्षेत्रों में मादक पदार्थों की तस्करी, आर्थिक अपराध और घुसपैठ के खिलाफ ज़ीरो टॉलरेंस की नीति के तहत आगे बढ़ रही है। अब पश्चिम बंगाल में राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा से जुड़े लंबित इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर कार्यों को प्राथमिकता के साथ पूरा किया जाएगा। साथ ही, यहाँ चतुष्कोणीय सुरक्षा ग्रिड स्थापित होने से सीमा पूरी तरह सुरक्षित और अभेद्य बनेगी। আজ শিলিগুড়িতে ভারত - বাংলাদেশ সীমান্ত সংক্রান্ত নিরাপত্তা বিষয়ক একটি বৈঠক করলাম। মোদী সরকার সীমান্তবর্তী এলাকায় মাদক পাচার, অর্থনৈতিক অপরাধ এবং অনুপ্রবেশের বিরুদ্ধে জিরো টলারেন্স নীতি নিয়ে কাজ করছে। এখন পশ্চিমবঙ্গে জাতীয় নিরাপত্তার সঙ্গে যুক্ত দীর্ঘদিনের পরিকাঠামোগত কাজগুলিকে অগ্রাধিকারের ভিত্তিতে সম্পূর্ণ করা হবে। পাশাপাশি, এখানে চতুষ্কোণীয় নিরাপত্তা গ্রিড গড়ে তোলার মাধ্যমে সীমান্তকে সম্পূর্ণ নিরাপদ ও দুর্ভেদ্য করা হবে।
